messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nora Fields <nora.fields@cobalthealth.com>, Elliot Vance <elliot.vance@cobalthealth.com>

Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Cobalt Health — Sponsor recap: pilot acceptance, risk & procurement path

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the clarity from Nora and Elliot. I wanted to capture the commitments and open risks so we have a single source of truth heading into SOW and procurement. High-level summary below, followed by concrete next steps and owners.

Key business outcomes discussed
- Reduce time-to-insight for clinician-facing summarization by >60% (target: sub-250ms median inference for 512-token summaries).
- Replace manual triage for top-3 diagnosis classes to cut review time by 35% and reduce monthly FTE hours spent on repeat cases.
- Pilot must demonstrate no PHI leakage and a measurable fall-back when quota/latency thresholds are hit.

Primary pain points raised
- Current hosted models have unpredictable token costs and sporadic latency spikes during batch windows.
- Security/compliance team needs concrete evidence of isolation, audit logs, and KMS integration for secrets.
- Procurement wants a clear acceptance and rollback criteria before committing to reserved capacity.

Acceptance criteria for pilot (agreed-in-principle)
1) Two-week pilot run against dev dataset with performance telemetry and redline report.
2) Median latency <= 300ms, P95 <= 750ms for 512-token summaries under our pilot load profile.
3) No critical security gaps in the Security_QA.xlsx and successful KMS handshake (staging).
4) A go/no-go decision from the Cobalt sponsor at the end of pilot with a written acceptance note.

Top risks and mitigations
- Risk: On-prem network egress policies could delay model updates. Mitigation: pre-stage quantized model artifact and run a smoke harness during onboarding window.
- Risk: Procurement demands a stronger SLA than our standard pilot. Mitigation: offer a 30-day pilot SLA addendum and explicit fallbacks to a lower-cost model variant.

Next steps and owners
- Marcus: circulate draft SOW and security appendix (attached) — ETA 48 hours (Cobalt review).
- Lauren: prepare telemetry dashboard template and expected telemetry fields for Cobalt's security team to validate.
- Ben: run a quick smoke test on our staging with a 50-user load profile and share the trace sample.
- Nora/Elliot: confirm procurement stakeholders and whether finance needs a vendor form filled before SOW.

Attachments: Cobalt_SOW_Draft_v1.pdf, Security_QA.xlsx (see Drive link above).

If any of the items above are off from what you heard, flag them and I will update. Otherwise I’ll push an editable SOW to the Drive and ping procurement next week.

Best,
Marcus

Marcus — thanks for the crisp recap. This aligns with what we heard internally. A few clarifications and confirmations: 

1) Acceptance criteria: we agree to the telemetry thresholds but need the P95 target in writing in the SOW (our legal will flag numeric SLAs otherwise).
2) Security: our InfoSec wants the audit-log format and retention schedule — can Lauren include a sample log export schema?
3) Procurement: I’ve looped in procurement@cobalthealth.com who will send our vendor packet and expected payment terms. We typically need net-60, but I can push for net-45 for pilots.

We are comfortable proceeding to a draft SOW and a staging smoke test. I’ll aim to give a definitive sponsor decision within three business days after the pilot concludes.

Nora

VP, Clinical Ops — Cobalt Health

- I’ve sketched the telemetry fields Nora asked for: request_id, model_variant, seq_len, client_kv_id, latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, cpu_gpu_util_pct, cache_hit_rate, error_class. I’ll drop a CSV template into the Drive.
- For the audit log export schema: retention default 90 days (we can lengthen for dedicated/private deployments). I’ll include the JSON schema and a sample export in the Security_QA.xlsx.
- Smoke test plan: Ben and I will run a 50-user profile against staging tomorrow at 10am PT and share traces + an anonymized transcript. Ben, please confirm the harness start time.

I’ll also prepare an appendix for the SOW that describes fallback behavior: if median latency exceeds 500ms for three contiguous 5-minute windows we gracefully switch to a compact model and emit an incident to Cobalt’s on-call.

-Lauren

Quick post-smoke update and one escalation item for leadership:

- Smoke test (50-user profile) completed 15 May — attached trace and 10 anonymized sample transcripts uploaded to Drive. Median latency: 282ms; P95: 680ms — within the pilot targets. Token spend on the test was slightly higher than projected due to longer-than-expected system prompts; we’ve flagged prompt-length as a controllable variable.
- Security QA: KMS handshake completed successfully in staging; audit-log export sample included in Security_QA.xlsx. No critical red flags found.
- Escalation: Procurement asked for a clause that allows a 30-day termination right for pilot if latency or cost exceed agreed thresholds, and they want a named Redwood contact for escalation beyond Luke in OCs.

Action requested from leadership (Kimberly / Marcus):
1) Confirm whether we can accept a 30-day pilot termination clause with a capped termination fee (recommended: pro-rata usage + $5k admin) or propose an alternative.
2) Approve Luke (Ops) as the primary on-call for the pilot and provide a backup contact from leadership who can be looped in for SLA disputes.

If we greenlight the clause, I’ll fold it into the SOW and re-upload for Cobalt procurement.

Thanks,
Ben
